**Hypothesis (EN):** The variable is **SES (Socioeconomic Status)**. The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024 (base model, highly significant) to 0.0923 (statistically insignificant) when both SES and academic characteristics are included in the analysis: SES's association with degree completion is largely explained by academic characteristics (class rank percentile and, to a lesser extent, ASVAB ability), so once they are controlled, SES has little or no independent effect on BA completion.

**Hipótesis (ES):** El efecto de SES (estatus socioeconómico) sobre BA degree completion disminuye de 0.5024 a 0.0923 y pierde significancia cuando se incluyen SES y características académicas: la asociación de SES con la graduación universitaria se explica en gran parte por las características académicas (percentil de clase y capacidad ASVAB), por lo que al controlarlas SES no tiene efecto independiente relevante.

**Workflow:** (1) Carga e inspección de nls_ses_processed.csv (n=8,773; BA=1 en 236 casos, 2.69%; 0 missing). (2) Regresión logística (logit) para cada una de las 8 variables como candidata: modelo base (candidata sola) vs. modelos completos (candidata + SES + características académicas, con 3 variantes de academics: ABILITY+PERCENTILE, solo ABILITY, solo PERCENTILE), en escala original y estandarizada. (3) Solo SES reproduce el patrón 0.5024→0.0923 (positivo y significativo → pequeño y no significativo). (4) Análisis de sensibilidad: PERCENTILE como cuartiles, submuestra de mujeres, VIF (1.27–2.26, colinealidad moderada sin problemas).

payload.hypothesis: The effect of SES (socioeconomic status) on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024 (base model, highly significant, OR≈1.6) to 0.0923 (statistically insignificant) when both SES and academic characteristics are included in the analysis: SES's association with degree completion is largely explained by academic characteristics (class rank percentile / ASVAB ability), so after controlling for them SES has little or no independent effect on BA completion.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded data/nls_ses_processed.csv (n=8773, 9 variables, 0 missing; BA completed in 236 cases, 2.69%). 2) Fit logistic (logit) regressions treating each of the 8 variables as the candidate: base model (candidate alone) vs full models (candidate + SES + academic characteristics; academics variants: ABILITY+PERCENTILE, ABILITY only, PERCENTILE only), in original and standardized scales. 3) Only SES reproduces the 0.5024 -> 0.0923 attenuation pattern (base b=0.4729, p=1e-08; full with class rank b=0.0814, p=0.372, insignificant). 4) Sensitivity: PERCENTILE as quartiles (b=0.1073, p=0.234), female subsample (0.4995 -> 0.1082, p=0.379), VIF checks (1.27-2.26). Conclusion: SES is the variable whose effect on BA completion is diluted to insignificance once SES and academic characteristics are in the model.
